Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

title: Document trusted publishing setup, including immutable subject claims
description:
Fixes #72.

GitHub repos created on or after 2026-07-15 issue OIDC tokens with [immutable subject claims](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-23-immutable-subject-claims-for-github-actions-oidc-tokens/) (`my-org@123456/my-repo@789012` instead of `my-org/my-repo`). Connect accepts either form in a trusted publisher's **Repository** field, but it has to match what the repo actually produces — get it wrong and the token exchange fails with an HTTP 400 while the configuration looks correct. Nothing in this repo said so.

## README

New **Trusted publishing** section, linked from the prerequisites list, the feature-support table, and the `deploy` auth docs:

- What to enter when adding a trusted publisher in the Connect UI (**Repository**, **Audience**).
- **Immutable subject claims** — both claim formats, which repos use which, and how to get the value. The reliable way is `gh api repos/$ORG/$REPO/actions/oidc/customization/sub` (reports what the repo actually produces, needs admin); the fallback builds the immutable form from owner/repo IDs, as in the issue.
- **Configuring a trusted publisher from the command line** — `posit connect login` as a human (a trusted-publishing credential can't manage trusted publishers), then `POST v1/content/$GUID/trusted-publishers` via `posit connect api`, plus list/revoke.

## `setup-connect-deploy` skill

New **Step 3a**, reached only when the user chooses trusted publishing, that offers to authorize the repository on Connect:

1. Determine `repository` by asking GitHub for the subject claim prefix, with the ID-based fallback when the endpoint 403s. If the prefix isn't `repo:`-shaped (customized claim template), it stops and points at a Custom OpenID Connect publisher instead of registering something that can't match.
2. Have the user run the interactive `posit connect login` themselves.
3. POST the publisher, confirming the JSON first.

Error handling maps 402/403/404 to license, permissions, and server-too-old respectively, recommending API-key auth in each case. Step 6's summary now reports the registered `repository` value so a later repo rename is a known breaking change.

Docs only — no action or package code changed.

title: docs: point Trusted Publishing setup at the Source tab
description:
README "Getting started" step 2 sent readers to the "Access" tab to enable Trusted Publishing. In current Connect that section lives on the "Source" tab, alongside the active bundle and runtime versions. The `setup-connect-deploy` skill was already corrected in #77; this is the last remaining reference.

Fixes #81

title: Decide requirements generation from files present, not app mode
description:
`generate-requirements.sh` now branches only on which files are in the working directory, and a missing dependency source is a no-op instead of an `exit 1`.

`posit connect deploy` already decides whether content needs a `requirements.txt`, and it does so more precisely than an `app_mode` lookup can: it inspects the Python environment for a `jupyter-engine` Quarto doc but not a `knitr-engine` one, and never for Node.js. When one is required and missing, it raises an error naming the file.

That removes the reason for `needs_requirements`, so it comes out of `AppType`, `resolve_app_type`, the CLI output, and the deploy step's `if:` condition, along with `REQUIREMENTS_DEPLOY_TYPES`.

One case the `app_mode` gate got wrong and this fixes: a `knitr-engine` Quarto doc with no Python anywhere resolved to `needs_requirements=true` and failed at the generate step with "No uv.lock or pyproject.toml file found."

Fixes #82.

title: Skip requirements generation for non-Python content
description:
Fixes #78.

Deploying Node.js content without a `manifest.json` failed at the "Generate requirements.txt if needed" step, which demanded a Python dependency source (`requirements.txt`, `uv.lock`, or `pyproject.toml`) for every app type, even though the resolved deploy subcommand (`posit connect deploy nodejs`) needs none.

`resolve_app_type` now also reports `needs_requirements`, mirroring the existing `needs_quarto` pattern, and `deploy/action.yml` gates the requirements step on it: true for the mapped Python/Quarto deploy types and fall-through `python-*`/`jupyter-*` app modes, false for manifests and everything else (e.g. `nodejs`). `generate-requirements.sh` itself is unchanged.

To verify: run the deploy action against existing Node.js content (app_mode `nodejs`) with no `manifest.json` in the app directory. Before this change the run failed with "No uv.lock or pyproject.toml file found"; now the step is skipped and the deploy proceeds.

title: fix: parse rsconnect-args with shell quoting so values can contain spaces
description:
## Bug

`deploy/scripts/deploy.sh` expands the `rsconnect-args` input unquoted:

```bash
posit connect deploy "$APP_TYPE" ... ${RSCONNECT_ARGS:-} "$DEPLOY_TARGET" ...
```

Plain Bash word-splitting (IFS) with no quote parsing means `rsconnect-args: --title "My App"` reaches the CLI as three tokens — `--title`, `"My` (with the literal quote), and `App"` — and the click-based CLI fails with `Got unexpected extra argument`. There's no way to pass an argument value containing whitespace.

This matters in practice: until [posit-dev/rsconnect-python#835](https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/issues/835) is fixed, passing `--title` matching the content's exact title is the only way to deploy a manifest under trusted publishing, and content titles routinely contain spaces.

Fixes #79

## Fix

Follows the existing `EXTRA_FILES` pattern (newline-delimited passing, since GitHub Actions outputs can't safely carry arbitrary whitespace/quoting):

- New `connect_actions.rsconnect_args` module: `parse_rsconnect_args()` splits the raw string with `shlex.split` (POSIX shell quoting rules), raising `RsconnectArgsError` on malformed input (e.g. an unbalanced quote).
- New `resolve-rsconnect-args` CLI subcommand (`cli.py`) reads `INPUT_RSCONNECT_ARGS`, parses it, and writes the result as a newline-delimited `rsconnect_args` `GITHUB_OUTPUT` value (same heredoc-style multi-line output `extra_files` already uses). Parse errors print `Error: ...` to stderr and exit 1.
- `deploy/action.yml`: new "Parse rsconnect-args" step runs the subcommand before the deploy step; the deploy step's `RSCONNECT_ARGS` env now comes from this step's output instead of the raw input.
- `deploy/scripts/deploy.sh`: reads the newline-delimited value into an `RSCONNECT_ARGS_ARR` array (mirroring the existing `EXTRA_FILE_ARGS` loop) and expands it as `"${RSCONNECT_ARGS_ARR[@]}"` instead of unquoted `${RSCONNECT_ARGS:-}`.
- `README.md`: documented that `rsconnect-args` supports shell-style quoting, e.g. `--title "My App"`.

Backward compatible: simple space-separated args like `--verbose --new` parse and behave identically to the old unquoted expansion (verified against the existing e2e workflow's `rsconnect-args: --override-python-version ...` usage).

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — all 77 tests pass, including new unit tests in `tests/test_rsconnect_args.py` (parsing: empty input, simple flags, double/single quoted values with spaces, mixed args, unbalanced-quote error) and `tests/test_cli.py` (new `resolve-rsconnect-args` subcommand: simple flags, quoted values, empty input, parse-error exit code).
- [x] `shellcheck deploy/scripts/deploy.sh` — clean, no warnings.

title: Fail with R-tailored error when R content lacks a manifest.json
description:
## Problem

Deploying an R project (with `renv.lock`) without a `manifest.json` failed with a Python-specific error from `generate-requirements.sh`:

```
No uv.lock or pyproject.toml file found. Please run 'uv sync' ...
```

The action effectively assumed Python content whenever `manifest.json` was absent, producing a misleading message that pointed R users toward `uv`/`pyproject.toml`.

## Fix

Rather than sniffing files (`renv.lock`, `.R`, `DESCRIPTION`, …), this uses the signal the architecture already treats as authoritative: the Connect content record's `app_mode`, fetched in the "Determine app type" step. That step runs **before** `generate-requirements.sh`, so gating there fails fast with a clear message and never reaches the Python path.

`resolve_app_type` now recognizes R app modes (`shiny`, `rmd-shiny`, `rmd-static`, `api`) and raises an R-tailored error explaining that R content must be deployed from a `manifest.json` generated via `rsconnect::writeManifest()`. A present `manifest.json` still short-circuits, so the supported R deploy path works unchanged.

## Notes

- `generate-requirements.sh` is untouched — its "no sources" error is now only reachable for genuinely Python-shaped content, where the message is appropriate.
- `quarto-static` still maps to `quarto` (Connect renders R-or-Python Quarto itself); `quarto-shiny` still falls through unchanged as before.

## Tests

Added parametrized tests asserting each R mode errors with R/`manifest.json`/`writeManifest` guidance and no `uv`/`pyproject` mention, plus a test that a manifest still deploys R content. All 60 non-network unit tests pass.

Fixes #69

title: test: cover TOML-based config resolution in the e2e deploy suite
description:
Closes #32.

## What

The `e2e-deploy` job only exercised **tier 1** of config resolution (explicit `connect-server` + `content-guid` inputs). The TOML-driven resolution paths — the headline "commit the Posit Publisher TOML and let the action pick everything up" workflow — had no end-to-end coverage.

This adds two deploy legs that run with **no** explicit `connect-server`/`content-guid` and resolve everything from a deployment TOML:

- **Tier 3** — a single TOML auto-detected under `.posit/publish/deployments/`.
- **Tier 2** — a TOML at a non-default path named via the `deployment-file` input.

Both reuse the prod record (already `python-fastapi`) via a **manifest-free** app copy, so they run through the `app_mode`-lookup path — the one that actually consumes the resolved `entrypoint` (the manifest path ignores it) — and prove the resolved server feeds `login.sh` and the resolved GUID + entrypoint feed `deploy.sh`, through the real `working-directory`/`INPUT_*` plumbing. Each asserts a non-empty, non-draft `content-url` and an incremented bundle count.

## Scope note

Issue #32 predates #36, which rewrote config resolution from `resolve-config.sh`/`parse-deployment-toml.py` into the unit-tested `src/connect_actions/config.py`. As a result the resolution **logic** and every **error case** (missing dir, zero/multiple TOMLs, missing file, non-zero exit + `Error:` message) are already thoroughly covered by `tests/test_config.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`. Those error cases need no live Connect, so they're left to the unit suite rather than duplicated in the (Connect-dependent, matrixed) e2e job. `tests/e2e/README.md` documents the new legs and cross-references the unit tests.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest` — 41 passed.
- Workflow YAML validated.
- The new legs themselves require CI (a live Connect + the `CONNECT_LICENSE` secret), so they'll run on this PR across the version matrix.

title: test: run e2e suite across a Connect version matrix (#33)
description:
Closes #33

Runs the end-to-end deploy suite against a matrix of Connect versions so version-specific regressions surface early, and switches the workflow's own Connect calls from `curl` to the `posit` CLI (per the follow-up ask on the issue).

## Version matrix

- `strategy.matrix.connect-version: ["2025.06.0", "2025.12.0", "release"]`, `fail-fast: false`, feeding `with-connect`'s `version` input.
- **Floor is 2025.06.0**: the suite exercises a draft deploy, which the action requires 2025.06.0+ for. Git provenance metadata needs 2025.12.0, but the action degrades gracefully below that (#34 / #49), so the 2025.06.0 leg still runs the full suite — just without metadata.
- `release` tracks the latest Connect build.
- Each leg creates its own content records against its own ephemeral server, so the draft-deploy PR comment (matched on GUID + host) and cleanup (filtered by `connect-server`) don't cross-interfere.

## curl → posit CLI

- Adds a `Set up posit CLI` step and replaces every `curl …/__api__/…` call with `posit connect api …`, which reads `CONNECT_SERVER`/`CONNECT_API_KEY` from the environment the steps already set — no login step needed. Covers create-records, the Python-version lookup, all bundle-count verifies, and cleanup verify. No `curl`/`jq` left in the workflow.

title: Gate version-dependent features on Connect version (#48)
description:
Closes #48
Closes #46 
Closes #30 
Closes #34 
Closes #23

Reads the Connect server version (`posit connect api server_settings -q .version`) on each run and adapts to what the server supports, with clear errors where the feature can't work and graceful degradation where it can be skipped.

## Behavior

| Feature | Minimum version | On older / unknown servers |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted Publishing (OIDC) | 2026.07.0 + Enhanced/Advanced license | **Fails on login** with a clear message; points to `connect-api-key` (#46, #23) |
| Draft PR previews (`draft: true`) | 2025.06.0 | **Fails fast** with a clear error; tells the user to set `draft: false` (#30) |
| Git provenance metadata | 2025.12.0 | **Silently skipped**; deploy still succeeds (#34) |

For draft/metadata the action reads the version and gates up front. For Trusted Publishing there is deliberately no version pre-check: the version alone isn't authoritative (it can't see the Enhanced/Advanced license or whether a trusted publisher is configured for the content), so `posit connect login` is the real check and `login.sh` prints a clear error covering all the requirements when it fails.

When the admin has hidden the server version, the deploy path degrades safely: it skips metadata (never risks failing the upload) and does not block drafts (lets the attempt surface its own error).

## Implementation

- **`src/connect_actions/versions.py`** — new pure, tested module: `parse_version`, `supports`, and per-feature minimum versions (`drafts`, `metadata`).
- **`cli.py`** — `check-deploy-features` subcommand that reads env, emits GitHub annotations, and writes `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, following the existing "logic in importable functions, CLI does I/O" convention.
- **`deploy/action.yml`** — a "Check Connect capabilities" step after login gates drafts and sets `send_metadata`; **`deploy.sh`** passes `--metadata` only when supported.
- **`scripts/login.sh`** — clear error on OIDC login failure explaining the Trusted Publishing requirements.
- **Docs** — new "Connect version requirements" section in the README, plus `SKILL.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the e2e README updated.

## Testing

`uv run pytest` — 41 passed (version parsing, feature gating, and the deploy-features CLI subcommand).

title: Use the posit CLI for Connect auth and API requests
description:
Closes #25.

Routes all Connect interaction through the [`posit` CLI](https://github.com/posit-dev/posit-cli) (which mounts the full `rsconnect-python` command set under `posit connect` and adds a `gh api`-style `posit connect api` raw REST client), anchored on a shared **login** step so no downstream step has to carry a server URL or API key around.

## What changed

**New `scripts/login.sh`** — logs the CLI in and stores the credential as the *default* server (rsconnect's server store, a file under `$HOME` that persists across composite steps):
- With `connect-api-key` → `posit connect add --set-default`
- Without → fetches a GitHub OIDC token and runs `posit connect login`, which performs the RFC 8693 token exchange and stores the minted key. This replaces the ~130-line hand-rolled `get-api-key.sh`.

**`deploy/`**

title: feat: Support PR previews across multiple Connect servers
description:
Closes #38.

## Problem

Both actions assumed one Connect server + content GUID per PR:

- **deploy** found the preview comment by a generic marker (`Preview deployed to Connect`) and updated the *first* match. With two deploy steps (two environments), the second clobbered the first comment and merged unrelated bundle IDs.
- **cleanup-previews** took a single `connect-server`/`content-guid` and deleted every bundle scraped from *all* preview comments against that one server — so bundles on other servers leaked, and under OIDC you had to pass the server up front.

## Key insight

The draft preview URL already encodes everything we need. rsconnect builds it as `dashboard_url + "/draft/{bundle}"`, and Connect's `dashboard_url` is `{server}/connect/#/apps/{guid}`. So **server + GUID + bundle id all come from the URL** — no comment-format change required. The existing `<!-- preview-bundles:… -->` block still accumulates every bundle across pushes.

## Changes

- **`deploy/action.yml`** — match the existing comment by marker **and** content GUID, so each environment owns its own comment. Name the server host in the heading (`(connect.example.com)`) to distinguish environments.
- **`cleanup-previews/action.yml`** — restructured into resolve → oidc → delete:
  - `resolve` reads PR comments, parses server/GUID/bundles from each preview URL, groups by server, and picks the target server from the `connect-server` input, infers it when there's only one, or fails with a clear "one step per server" message when there are several.
  - `oidc` (existing `get-api-key.sh`, unchanged) runs only when no API key is provided, using the resolved server.
  - `delete` deletes the bundles and posts a per-server summary.
  - Dropped the now-redundant `content-guid`, `deployment-file`, `path` inputs and the config-resolution/uv steps (cleanup no longer touches the Python package). **Breaking change to cleanup's interface** (beta).
- **`README.md`** — documented multi-server previews and simplified the OIDC cleanup example (single-server cleanup needs no `connect-server`).
- **`.github/workflows/test.yml`** — added a PR-guarded e2e step that cleans up the draft preview and asserts the bundle is deleted.

## Notes / deviations

- The e2e cleanup step passes `connect-server` explicitly rather than relying on inference: the test PR accumulates preview comments from prior CI runs (each on a fresh ephemeral Connect/GUID), which would otherwise trip the "multiple servers" failure. It still exercises the full parse → delete → summary path.
- The deploy comment now calls `new URL(previewUrl).host`, which throws on an empty URL (previously it rendered a broken link). A successful draft deploy always has a URL, so this fails loudly instead of posting garbage.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` — 14/14 green (config package untouched).
- All action/workflow YAML validates.
- e2e cleanup step added for the single-server happy path; multi-server logic covered by review (can't be e2e-tested with one Connect).

title: test: add e2e deploy sanity check against a real Connect
description:
Closes #3.

First slice of issue #3: an end-to-end sanity check that the `deploy` action can actually deploy to a real Connect, so we have coverage at the actions interface before refactoring the bash scripts. Also makes draft deploys explicitly controllable so the test can cover both paths.

## `draft` input

`deploy` gains a `draft` input that controls whether the deploy is a draft (preview) bundle. It defaults to the prior behavior — `true` on `pull_request` events, `false` otherwise — but can now be set explicitly (publish from a PR, or stage a draft from a push). `deploy.sh` keys the `--draft` flag off this instead of the event name, and the PR preview comment is gated on `draft == true` so an explicit production deploy from a PR doesn't post a (wrong) preview link.

## e2e test (`.github/workflows/test.yml`)

One `e2e-deploy` job:

1. Starts a real Connect via [`posit-dev/with-connect`](https://github.com/posit-dev/with-connect) (start-only mode).
2. Creates two empty content records via `curl` to `/__api__/v1/content`.
3. Generates a `manifest.json` for the `test/e2e/fastapi-app` fixture at runtime via `rsconnect write-manifest`.
4. Runs the local `deploy` action twice — `draft: false` (production) and `draft: true` (preview).
5. Verifies each set a non-empty `content-url`, that the URL is a draft URL **only** for the draft deploy, and that a bundle landed on the record.

## Notes

- **Manifest path, not the regular app-mode path.** A freshly created record has `app_mode = "unknown"`, which `deploy.sh` can't map to an `rsconnect` subcommand. The `manifest.json` path takes a brand-new record straight to deployed.
- **`--no-verify` on the draft deploy.** A brand-new record has no *active* bundle, so rsconnect's default post-deploy verification (a GET of the content's main URL) has nothing to reach. The job's own bundle/URL checks are the real assertion there.
- Runs on push to `main`, `pull_request`, and `workflow_dispatch`.
- Requires a `CONNECT_LICENSE` secret (file contents) for `with-connect`.
- Connect is pinned to `2025.09.0` with `--override-python-version 3.12`; adjust if needed.

title: Pass rich git metadata to rsconnect deploy
description:
## Summary

Adds `--metadata` arguments to the `rsconnect deploy` command so that Connect receives accurate, useful source information instead of "dirty" SHAs and "HEAD" branch names.

**Metadata passed on every deploy:**
- `source=github-actions` — distinguishes CI-deployed bundles
- `source_commit` — the actual commit SHA (PR head SHA on pull requests, `github.sha` on push)
- `source_branch` — the PR head branch ref on PRs, `github.ref_name` on push
- `source_author` — the `github.actor` username
- `source_github_actions_run` — URL to the workflow run

**Additional metadata on pull requests:**
- `source_pull_request` — the PR number
- `source_description` — the PR title

**On push to default branch:**
- `source_description` — the first line of the commit message

### Implementation notes
- Uses a bash array for `METADATA_ARGS` to correctly handle values with spaces (e.g., PR titles)
- Extracts only the first line of commit messages for `source_description`
- `GITHUB_SHA` is explicitly set to `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` on PRs to get the actual commit, not the merge commit

Closes #12
